name: arborium
description: Rust batteries-included tree-sitter highlighting with many bundled grammars and WASM/browser support

host-language.comment: Rust crate. The npm package @arborium/arborium is a JS/WASM wrapper over the Rust host, so it is counted under Bindings / Ports. Grammar parsers are C generated by tree-sitter.

form-factor.comment: Rust library, the official arborium-cli crate, and the npm package that ships a WASM host plus per-language WASM grammar plugins. The drop-in script tag auto-highlights code blocks, and the HTML uses custom elements like <a-k>, but neither is a web component.

license.comment: MIT OR Apache-2.0. Vendored grammars keep their original licences (listed in LICENSES.md). The README says permissively licensed grammars (MIT, Apache-2.0, CC0, Unlicense) are the default set.

package.comment: Also published on npm as @arborium/arborium, along with per-language grammar packages.

documentation.comment: The project site has the demo, usage guide (Rust, npm ESM, script tag, rustdoc), and language, theme and tag catalogs. The API reference is on docs.rs.

first-release.comment: The crate was first published on crates.io on 2025-12-04. The launch post is dated 2025-12-13.

latest-version.comment: Checked 2026-11-18. Released 2026-08-28. The npm package is at the same version.

engine-model.comment: Runs tree-sitter parsers with highlights/injections queries, using patched forks of tree-sitter and tree-sitter-highlight. Grammars are generated with tree-sitter 0.26.

regex-engine.comment: Grammars are generated tree-sitter parsers, not regex rules.

embedded-languages.comment: Uses tree-sitter injections (injections.scm). Config.max_injection_depth defaults to 3 and covers HTML with CSS/JS and Markdown code blocks. In Rust, the injected language's feature must be enabled. In the browser, the host loads the extra grammar plugins; a standalone per-language npm module cannot resolve injections on its own.

language-auto-detection.comment: The library's detect_language works only from the file path or extension. The CLI also checks a small hard-coded list of shebangs (python, node, ruby, perl, sh/bash, zsh, fish, php). Neither guesses the language from general content.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: detect_language maps a file extension to a canonical language id. The npm package also exports detectLanguage and handles language-* classes.

resumable-line-state.comment: No per-line saved-state API. Each parse covers the whole document.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Only in the JS/WASM package. Since 2.18 (commit of 2026-05-31), Grammar.createSession() returns a Session whose applyEdit(newText, edit) reparses while reusing the unchanged parts of the previous tree. The Rust API (CompiledGrammar.parse, Highlighter) does not document any edit or old-tree API.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Highlights come from tree-sitter queries on the syntax tree. Spans keep the raw capture name, and the theme slots include distinctions such as builtin function, method and parameter. Caveat: the locals query is accepted but 'currently unused', so references are not resolved to their definitions.

bundled-languages.comment: Count of lang-* feature flags enabled by all-languages in 2.18.2, checked 2026-11-18. typescript and tsx are counted separately. The project site says 101 and the README says about 70; both look out of date. Each language sits behind its own feature flag.

grammar-format.comment: Tree-sitter grammars with highlights/injections/locals .scm queries, vendored as per-language crates under langs/.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Takes any tree-sitter Language plus query strings. The project hand-picks upstream grammars, regenerates them with tree-sitter 0.26, and adds highlight queries where they were missing.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Rust: GrammarStore::insert registers a third-party CompiledGrammar (built from a tree-sitter Language and queries), and it then goes through the same lookup as the built-ins. JS: registerGrammar(jsModule, wasm) registers a grammar module that is already loaded.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: In the browser, loadGrammar fetches each grammar's WASM plugin from the CDN on first use. In Rust, grammars are linked in at compile time by feature flag, but they are 'compiled on first access and cached'.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Grammars are tree-sitter grammars regenerated with tree-sitter 0.26, with highlight queries hand-added or fixed. Open issues report poor highlighting for SCSS (#194), Elixir (#193), Clojure (#192) and F# (#182, broken since 2.14.0). Haskell (#183) was fixed by switching to the tree-sitter-grammars Haskell grammar. No mainstream TS/Rust/Python reports were seen. Rated 4 rather than 5 because of these regressions in less common languages.

bundled-themes.comment: 33 built-in themes in 2.18.2 (22 dark, 11 light), including Catppuccin, Dracula, Tokyo Night, GitHub, Gruvbox, Solarized and rustdoc. Checked 2026-11-18. The site still says 32. The CLI README mentions 12 themes for ANSI.

theme-format.comment: Rust themes are `Theme` structs (built-ins are functions in theme::builtin; custom ones via Theme::new and set_style). The npm package ships each theme as a CSS file, and Theme::to_css generates CSS. The built-ins are adapted from Helix-style TOML files at build time; no public TOML loader is documented in the default API, and there is no Helix TOML tag.

token-classification.comment: Spans carry tree-sitter capture names. arborium-theme maps nvim-treesitter and Helix capture names onto a fixed set of theme slots and short HTML tags (e.g. keyword -> <a-k>).

css-class-output.comment: The default output uses custom elements (<a-k>, <a-f>) styled by stylesheets. HtmlFormat::ClassNames and ClassNamesWithPrefix produce <span class="keyword">. There is no inline-style HTML mode.

multi-theme-output.comment: base.css ('handles light/dark switching — include this + one light theme + one dark theme') uses per-tag CSS variables, switching on prefers-color-scheme or :root[data-theme=light|dark]. Theme::to_css takes a selector prefix such as [data-theme="mocha"] so several themes can share one render.

public-token-api.comment: Highlighter::highlight_spans returns 'raw spans (for custom rendering)'. The advanced module exposes CompiledGrammar::parse, which returns a ParseResult with spans and injections. In JS, grammar.parse() and session.parse() return spans with UTF-16 offsets.

ir-kinds.comment: A flat list of Span {start, end, capture, pattern_index} (spans may overlap and are deduplicated at render time), plus Injection points. The syntax tree is not exposed through the highlighting API.

serializable-ir.comment: The Rust Span and ParseResult types implement only Clone, Debug and Eq-style traits; serde is not documented. In JS, spans are plain objects that could be JSON-stringified, but no serialization format is documented.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Spans carry only capture names. Callers can look up colours themselves with Theme::style(index) via the capture-to-slot mapping, but no API emits tokens with resolved styles. The resolved ANSI path (spans_to_ansi) outputs a finished string.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: Rust spans use UTF-8 byte offsets (start inclusive, end exclusive). The JS API returns UTF-16 code-unit offsets.

custom-formatter-api.comment: The advanced module is documented as the 'Advanced API for custom highlighting implementations': callers take raw spans and render them, reusing helpers such as html_escape and write_spans_as_html. There is no Formatter trait.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: No built-in line or range annotation mechanism. The options only cover injection depth, HTML format, and ANSI wrapping/padding/border.

output-formats.comment: HTML using custom elements (default) or class-name spans, and 24-bit true-colour ANSI via AnsiHighlighter / spans_to_ansi. There is no inline-style HTML output.

line-numbers.comment: Neither the HTML Config, AnsiOptions nor the CLI arguments (--lang, --html, --theme, input) offer line numbers.

streaming-output.comment: highlight_to_writer avoids building an intermediate String, but it still takes the complete source. No API emits output before the full input has been consumed.

terminal-ready.comment: AnsiHighlighter produces true-colour ANSI with themes. Options cover wrapping, padding, margins and a half-block border. arborium-cli outputs ANSI by default.

native-dependencies.comment: The Rust crate compiles the C tree-sitter runtime (a patched fork) and the C grammar parsers/scanners. The npm package ships arborium_host_bg.wasm (about 150 KB) and loads per-language WASM grammar plugins.

runs-in-browser.comment: Drop-in script tag or ESM module. Grammars are WASM plugins fetched from jsDelivr by default, and the CDN is configurable.

wasm-build.comment: Officially builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown, using arborium-sysroot to supply libc pieces (dlmalloc) to the C parsers, and publishes WASM packages to npm.

synchronous-api.comment: The Rust API is fully synchronous. In JS, loadGrammar and the convenience highlight() are async, but a loaded Grammar's parse() and session methods are synchronous. Grammar.highlight() is typed string | Promise<string>.

bindings-ports.comment: Official npm package @arborium/arborium (WASM, TypeScript types). A third-party Python binding, orgnizedmess/py-arborium, exists but has a single commit, 0 stars and no PyPI release, so it is not tagged.

core-package-size.comment: Size of the arborium 2.18.2 .crate on crates.io. This umbrella crate excludes the tree-sitter runtime and all per-language grammar crates, which are much larger. The npm @arborium/arborium 2.18.2 unpacked size is 482,370 bytes, including theme CSS and the 150 KB host WASM, but excluding grammar plugins.

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible comparative benchmark found. The npm description says 'high-performance' but gives no numbers.

initialization-cost.comment: Not measured. CompiledGrammar::new is documented as costly because it compiles queries, and the site says WASM grammar bundles 'are still large', which suggests a noticeable first-load cost in the browser. No figures found.

monthly-downloads.comment: crates.io recent_downloads (90 days) of 132,633 divided by 3, checked 2026-11-18. The npm downloads are not included (the npm page returned 403).

maintenance-status.comment: 45 releases since December 2025. The latest release and commits are from 2026-08-28, within 6 months of the 2026-11-18 check. The pace has slowed since spring 2026, and 34 issues are open.

documentation-quality.comment: The project site has a usage guide (Rust, npm, script tag, rustdoc), language/theme/tag catalogs and a live demo, and docs.rs has an API reference with examples. Held back from 5 because there are no migration notes and the README and site counts are stale (70 or 101 languages, 32 themes).

notable-users.value: dodeca (bearcove's static site generator); per-crate docs.rs/rustdoc highlighting of non-Rust code blocks via --html-in-header (arborium-docsrs-demo); cmdcolin's blog (CLI at build time)
notable-users.comment: No large independent adopter found. docs.rs itself has not adopted it; it is an opt-in per crate, and the rustdoc PR (rust-lang/rust #149944) proposed in the launch post was not verified as merged.

bus-factor.comment: Created and mostly committed by Amos Wenger (fasterthanlime) under his bearcove org. There are occasional outside contributors (language PRs merged in #200, #165, #215).
